authoring_basis.note: Teacher guide activity 1 stresses that parts must be equal before naming halves and quarters.

description: Counts parts of a shape without checking that the parts are equal, so an unequal split is named as halves, quarters or tenths.
distinguishing_evidence: chooses the unequal-parts representation while rejecting equal-parts distractors with a different shaded count
label_si: අසමාන කොටස් ද භාග ලෙස ගැනීම
observable_error_patterns: selects a shape split into unequal parts as showing the target fraction
sorts an unequally split shape into the target-fraction group
remediation_notes: compare equal and unequal partitions of the same shape before counting

authoring_basis.note: Part-to-part naming is a widely reported early fraction error; a literature citation must be added by the reviewer.

description: Writes the number of shaded parts over the number of unshaded parts (part-to-part) instead of over the total number of equal parts.
distinguishing_evidence: denominator equals the count of unshaded parts rather than the total
label_en: Compares shaded parts with unshaded parts
label_si: පාට කළ කොටස් පාට නොකළ කොටස් සමඟ සැසඳීම
remediation_notes: count every equal part, shaded and unshaded, to find the bottom number

authoring_basis.note: Researcher hypothesis based on figure-reading tasks in the textbook; needs teacher confirmation.

description: Uses the unshaded parts as the top number, naming the complement of the shaded amount.
distinguishing_evidence: answer equals the complement of the correct fraction within the same whole
remediation_notes: point to the shaded parts first and say what is being counted

authoring_basis.note: Researcher hypothesis; confirm with Grade 5 teachers.

description: Writes the total number of parts on top and the shaded count below.
distinguishing_evidence: both numbers are correct but their positions are swapped
label_en: Reverses the top and bottom numbers
label_si: උඩ සහ යට අංක මාරු කිරීම
remediation_notes: say the fraction aloud as 'shaded parts out of all equal parts'

authoring_basis.note: Researcher hypothesis; may also reflect not reading the fraction.

description: Reports the total number of objects instead of the number in the requested fraction of the set.
label_en: Gives the whole set as the answer
observable_error_patterns: puts all 20 objects in the box for 1/4 of 20
remediation_notes: separate the set into equal groups before answering

authoring_basis.note: Researcher hypothesis about operation choice; confirm with teachers.

description: Treats 'half' or 'quarter' as taking away 2 or 4 objects.
distinguishing_evidence: answer equals total minus the denominator
label_en: Subtracts the bottom number from the total
remediation_notes: show that a half is one of two equal groups, not two objects removed

description: Doubles the set for 'half', treating the 2 in 1/2 as a multiplier.
distinguishing_evidence: answer equals total times the denominator
remediation_notes: check that a half of a set is smaller than the set

authoring_basis.note: The textbook worked example builds 2/4 and 3/4 from one quarter.

description: Divides the set into four equal groups but ignores the top number, so 2/4 or 3/4 is answered as one group.
distinguishing_evidence: answer equals total divided by 4 when the top number is greater than 1
remediation_notes: after finding one quarter, take as many quarters as the top number shows

description: Divides the total by the top number of the fraction.
distinguishing_evidence: answer equals total divided by the numerator
remediation_notes: identify which number tells how many equal groups to make

authoring_basis.note: Researcher hypothesis; for 3/4 items the complement equals one quarter, so it cannot be separated from MAT-FRC-M08.

description: Gives the objects outside the requested fraction (the complement).
distinguishing_evidence: answer equals total minus the correct answer
remediation_notes: circle the requested groups and count only those

description: Writes the top and bottom numbers of a tenths fraction either side of a decimal point.
distinguishing_evidence: decimal contains the digits of both numbers separated by a point
label_en: Replaces the fraction bar with a decimal point
label_si: භාග ඉර දශම තිතක් ලෙස ලිවීම
remediation_notes: read the fraction as 'tenths' and place the count in the tenths place

description: Ignores the decimal point and treats 0.6 as 6.
distinguishing_evidence: answer equals the tenths digit as a whole number
label_en: Reads a decimal as a whole number
label_si: දශම සංඛ්‍යාව පූර්ණ සංඛ්‍යාවක් ලෙස කියවීම
remediation_notes: show 0.6 on a strip of ten equal parts

authoring_basis.note: Researcher hypothesis; hundredths are not taught in this unit, so this may also reflect guessing.

description: Places the tenths digit one place too far right, so 4/10 becomes 0.04 and 0.6 becomes 6/100.
distinguishing_evidence: answer is ten times too small
label_si: දහයෙන් පංගු සියයෙන් පංගු ලෙස ලිවීම
remediation_notes: say the decimal aloud as 'zero point six' and match it to six tenths

authoring_basis.note: Reserved fallback code shared across gamification catalogues.

description: Shared fallback when the response cannot distinguish a catalogued misconception.
distinguishing_evidence: no catalogued pattern explains the response
remediation_notes: use the least intrusive available scaffold

authoring_basis.note: Reserved non-diagnostic code for distractors without a misconception link.

description: Wrong option with no diagnostic link to a catalogued misconception.
distinguishing_evidence: no catalogued pattern predicts this option
remediation_notes: offer an independent retry before any scaffold
